passages.provision_quote: A firearm industry member shall not advertise, market, or arrange for placement of an advertising or marketing communication concerning any firearm-related product in a manner that is designed, intended, or reasonably appears to be attractive to minors.
passages.note: The chaptered text is the instrument of the vote; it prints the operative section but names no voter, so actor and tally sit on the vote page.

rows.reasoning: The only record is Lackey's No on AB 2571 (2021-2022), whose operative section bars a firearm industry member from marketing a firearm-related product "in a manner that is designed, intended, or reasonably appears to be attractive to minors" and sets no rule on who may own a firearm, which types are allowed, what a sale requires, or how permits to carry work. The rungs separate on exactly those things — "require universal background checks on every sale", "Add no new restrictions, and at most loosen rules on carrying", and the ownership and assault-style bans — so a vote on firearm advertising is adjacent to the dimension this ladder orders, and opposition to a commercial-speech restriction is consistent with several rungs at once. With no passage surviving V2, the row is blank.
